subject: Invoice epoch shift impacting April marketplace settlements
messages:
From: Marketplace Billing Ops <marketplace-billing@cloudvendor.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Invoice epoch shift affecting April settlements

Hi Vivek,

We discovered a batch of marketplace invoices where the usage epoch on a subset of metering events was encoded in seconds (epoch) but interpreted by our downstream aggregator as milliseconds. As a result ~11,200 usage lines from 2029-03-31 23:55:00 UTC through 2029-04-01 00:10:00 UTC were assigned to the wrong billing window and flowed into the April invoice set.

This has two customer-facing impacts we need your help with:
- Merchant attribution: some lines show as assigned to the seller entity for Acme Cloud Solutions but originated under a different merchant entity due to the epoch mismatch.
- VAT/GST treatment: the mis-assigned period changes the tax jurisdiction in a few EU transactions (small amounts, but needs correction).

We've attached a small manifest (epoch_shift_manifest.csv) with the usage IDs, original timestamps, and our suggested target invoice IDs. Can Redwood confirm the true merchant mapping for the affected usage IDs and whether you can issue retro credits or reissue corrected invoice lines?

Request: Can you confirm by EOD Wednesday if we can proceed with a credit memo and corrected payout for Acme?

Thanks,
Alyssa T.
Marketplace Billing Ops
CloudVendor Marketplace

Attachment: epoch_shift_manifest.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)

Alyssa—thanks for the heads-up and the manifest. I'm looping in Marissa (Finance ops) and Marcus (Accounting) to confirm entity mapping and retro credit options, and Priyom to validate the ingestion behavior on our side.

Quick asks to unblock:
1) Can you include a sample raw metering record (one full JSON row) for an affected usage_id so our ingestion team can reproduce the parse error?
2) Please confirm which seller entity IDs you expect to be the corrected targets (you included suggested invoice IDs, but we need seller-level entity IDs).
3) Any DocuSign/approval link you require for credits? If you need a PO or signed amendment from Acme, copy their finance contact into the thread.

We will triage and come back with a proposed reconciliation plan (credits + timing) by Thursday EOD PST. If this becomes material to April payouts we may need to delay the Acme payout by one settlement cycle while credits are applied.

—Vivek

Thanks, Alyssa and Vivek — I pulled the manifest and started a seller-entity cross-check against our ledger. Attached is a working file (seller-entity-mapping.xlsx) with our preliminary mapping and flags for lines where we have low confidence.

Immediate recommendations from Finance Ops:
- For lines where seller mapping is high confidence we can issue retro credit memos and re-attribute the revenue in the April ledger.
- For low-confidence lines (about ~320 rows), we need confirmation of order-level metadata (order_id, buyer_account_id) to avoid incorrect VAT reclaims. Please ask Acme to provide buyer_order references for those IDs.
- We should hold Acme’s payout for the affected settlement cycle until credits are processed to avoid double-payment exposure. If that is not acceptable, we can proceed with credit memos in the next cycle but it will delay tax corrections.

Marcus: can your team draft the credit memo template we can use so we can fast-track when mapping is confirmed?

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 04 Apr 2029 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice epoch shift affecting April settlements

Folks—quick technical update from infra/ingest: I pulled the raw sample and replayed it against our previous ingestion release. Root cause: a conversion path in the legacy aggregator interpreted the epoch field inconsistently when the payload included a "timestamp_ms" and a separate "timestamp" field. For ~2.4% of inbound records in that 15-minute window the parser chose the seconds field and then multiplied during downstream normalization, effectively shifting timestamps by a factor of 1,000 for a subset.

What I've validated:
- Affected usage_ids are enumerated in attached affected_usage_ids.txt (list, ~11,200 lines).
- There is no cross-tenant data exposure; all records belong to sellers in the manifest.
- Fix: deploy a small ingest patch to normalize epoch handling and re-run the aggregation job to re-bucket the affected events. Estimated time to run and validate: 18 hours.

Operational recommendation:
1) Run the ingest patch tomorrow morning (Fri 2029-04-05 02:00 UTC).
2) Recompute aggregator outputs and produce corrected invoice lines.
3) Finance to prepare credit memos and hold the April payout for Acme until verification is complete (or confirm alternative).

I'll coordinate the run and post logs to the Drive folder.

Attachment: affected_usage_ids.txt (text, 280KB)

Team—summary and proposed reconciliation plan based on the attachments and Priyom’s analysis. Please review and confirm by EOD Friday so we can execute next week.

Summary:
- Root cause: inconsistent epoch parsing on a small subset of events in our ingestion pipeline (confirmed by Priyom).
- Scope: ~11.2k usage lines across six seller entities; VAT exposure approx. €1,320 across two seller entities.
- No data leakage or PII exposure.

Proposed next steps (timeline):
1) Priyom to deploy ingest patch and re-run aggregation: target complete by Sat 2029-04-06 10:00 UTC.
2) Marissa + Marcus to draft retro credit memos for high-confidence mappings and prepare a separate review bucket for low-confidence rows (Marissa will request buyer_order ids from Acme). Target: draft memos ready Mon 2029-04-08.
3) Apply credits and reissue corrected invoice lines in the next settlement window. If Acme approves hold of the April payout, we will apply credits before payout and release corrected funds by Mon 2029-04-15.
4) For VAT adjustments, Redwood will provide a supplemental VAT schedule and supporting ledger entries; Acme should confirm whether they prefer a single consolidated VAT correction or per-invoice adjustments.

Questions for Acme/Marketplace Billing Ops:
- Do you approve the proposed timeline and either: (A) hold the April payout to allow in-cycle correction; or (B) proceed with a next-cycle correction and credits?
- Can Acme provide buyer_order references for the ~320 low-confidence rows by Monday 2029-04-08?

If we get sign-off, Marcus will publish the credit memo templates and Marissa will kick off the reconciliation. Priyom will post the run logs and corrected CSVs to the Drive folder.

Thanks all—
